title: Refining Sentence Embedding Model through Ranking Sentences Generation with Large Language Models
subcategory: LLM-synthesised ranking data with directional control for post-training sentence encoders
problem: LLM-generated sentence pairs ignore ranking information needed for fine-grained semantic distinctions; naive prompting yields ambiguous rankings.
architecture: Directionally controlled decoding: the next sentence's sampling combines the latent generation directions of the two previous sentences, producing ranking sentences with progressively increasing divergence; post-training of existing models (SynCSE, MultiCSR) with a loss that mixes ranking and semantic-similarity information (weight omega).
key_results: BERT-base: MultiCSR-r averages 81.33 and SynCSE-r 81.17 on seven STS tasks vs 80.61 and 80.13 before refinement.
strengths: Shows the value of ranking information in synthetic data.
Modest generation cost; ablations of each generation/post-training choice.

limitations.text: Selection and refinement of synthesised data are not addressed.
Depends on the hyperparameter omega; an adaptive scheme is future work.
